title: White and Black neighbors in St. John Parish
summary: She describes mixed communities in her country childhood and her father's relationship with a white man.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Do you have white people and Cala people in January in those days? Oh yeah, oh yeah, oh yeah.

Yeah, yeah. Well, St. John, this is white people here, this is white people there. From a little girl, I used to go to the grocery store there. It was Sim Street. It was two of me and a brother. It was Sim Street. Now, the old man, my father, if you are a good scientist, it's the man I met, about 18 years. And he's about to have a black one. And so, my father was his place. Now, you can only know the world, the only world, and all white people. Well, I was from young one to the old. Now, when somebody was sick home, and they all made their experience to be there, because they had to give thanks and live in their own mind. And when they asked, I said, this is my mother, you see my mother, this is a woman, a Indian woman. But his father, they couldn't stand a white man, and he still had two. A dog man, two daughters married, well, each one took a black man. This is my father, a picture of that. You see, in his days, during the Civil War, he fed the Civil War. And so, he had the men that were raised, had two sons. And he was coming up with that boy, they definitely lived with him. Them two slept together, they were together. When they went in the home, they went together. So, that meant that when, after the war, he had to stay so in the country, so it wasn't any way. You know what he said, Kay?
No, I'm not well appointed, I don't.

That was the richest white man out there. And he has the biggest white people. Where he sat down. That was the best. And empty. When they build a big school for the white folks. Him and my father have to top seat together. He couldn't speak French and my father couldn't speak English. They both speak Spanish. They do make a speech about the school. Then after they finish building a white school, they make for color. They both were at the same time. Now after the war, the colored people used to be the officer. My father put a white man and a colored man. Now that's the white man he raised, called Paul Bethlehem. And I was glad that they brought my father everything from the horse. My father was from the old horse. My father had ten new horses as I was coming up. Big white kids and everything. Reads, rise, who knows? He was God, he was born from the old man. And he never could finish the old horse until the Henry took him in church. And that's when we already got healed. Now all the children, grandchildren, we married boys children. We married, we all in the same. We were taught some of these things. Now all the children down there, and all the children, they all lived with me. I was always talking about the children. When were you born? I was born in 1893.
